answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so influence decays across poorly connected regions rather than accumulating from repeated endorsements. A sybil coalition typically appears as a sparse external cut with low conductance φ; Cheeger-style mixing bounds limit the walk mass that can escape it, while min-cut transitivity constrains mutually reinforcing attestations. Thus its aggregate voting weight remains bounded, whether its identifiers read fable, falcon, or sonnet.
